title: Thread Handoff: Mini-catalog of Customer Threads and Feature Seeds
summary: A compact handoff note synthesizing recent customer threads focused on latency, kv-cache behavior, model fallbacks, and small feature asks. Includes prioritized micro-proposals that can be scoped as 1-2 sprint spikes or quick engineering shims. Intended for PM + serving-runtime + SRE handoff before next planning sync.
body:
Purpose: capture discrete customer threads we triaged in July 2026, unify ask language, estimate impact/effort, and propose a small backlog of micro-features and runtime mitigations. Context: many customers are pushing long-chat, multimodal prompts and seeing latency spikes or sudden regens when fallback routing occurs. Also recurring asks around better observability of prefix cache hits and easier per-route rollout controls. This doc intentionally shortlists low-risk, high-signal items that can be validated with tiny experiments.

Observed themes and examples:
- Latency cliffs at scale: two mid-market customers (healthcare, e-commerce) reported elevated tail latency during long-sequence sessions when autoscaling and routing policies tripped over model variants. They saw increased token-cost and occasional timeouts.
- KV-cache opacity: enterprise customers asked for a per-request indicator (boolean + hit ratio) that shows if prefix/KV caching served majority of tokens in a response. Current console charts show aggregate cache savings but not request-level traces.
- Model-fallback churn: customers using region-aware routing experienced intermittent content regressions when requests fell back to smaller quantized variants; they want predictable degradation, not quality cliffs.
- Small UX asks: (1) per-route retry/backoff policy in the Console, (2) a one-click toggle to disable streaming on a route, (3) clearer quota-exhaustion messages in SDK errors.

Representative customer quotes (redacted):
- "We had a spike where 99.9th tail jumped and our chat feature timed out for some users — need a graceful fallback that doesn't blow up the conversation." — enterprise PM
- "We can't tell if we saved cost through caching on a given convo; the console numbers don't map back to our session id." — platform engineer
- "Fallback to that smaller quantized model changed responses in a way that feels like hallucination. We need a way to pin critical routes." — security lead

Prioritized mini-requests (seed backlog):
1) Request-level cache signal + session link
   - What: Emit a light metadata header/tag with each response: cache_hit:true|false and a confidence bucket (high|medium|low) plus an optional session_id passthrough for Console linking.
   - Why: Enables CS and customers to validate when caching reduced cost and identify sessions that did not benefit (root-cause).
   - Impact: High observability; low compute cost.
   - Rough effort: 3-5 dev days (runtime + Console minor UI line item).
   - Owner suggestion: serving-runtime + console team.

2) Graceful model-fallback policy (soft-degrade mode)
   - What: New routing policy that, when falling back to lower-tier model, automatically reduces generation length and turns on conservative decoding params (higher top-p/top-k restraint) for the first N tokens to avoid sudden hallucination.
   - Why: Keeps UX consistent while preserving uptime.
   - Impact: Medium customer satisfaction improvement for fallbacks.
   - Rough effort: 2 sprint spikes (runtime + policy).
   - Owner suggestion: runtime + platform-engineering.

3) Tail latency alarm + fast-shed playbook
   - What: Per-customer SLA profile that triggers an automated fast-shed action (e.g., degrade to cached prefix-only responses or short-circuit noncritical ops) when percentile tail breaches sustained threshold. Include runbook snippet.
   - Why: Prevents customer-visible timeouts and provides immediate mitigation.
   - Impact: High for customers sensitive to tail latencies.
   - Rough effort: SRE + console config work, 1-2 sprints.
   - Owner suggestion: site-reliability-engineering.

4) Per-route retry/backoff and streaming toggle in Console
   - What: UI controls to set retry/backoff policy and to toggle streaming for a specific route. Also expose SDK error mapping to clearer messages.
   - Why: Operational control reduces need for CS interventions.
   - Impact: Low friction improvement, broad adoption.
   - Rough effort: 1 sprint UI + small backend flag.
   - Owner suggestion: product/console-and-rollouts + developer-experience.

5) Quick diagnostic export for CS handoff
   - What: A single-click download that packages last N requests for a session (headers, model variant, cache flags, latencies) with an anonymized customer identifier for engineering investigations.
   - Why: Speeds troubleshooting and reduces back-and-forth.
   - Impact: High time-savings for CS/eng.
   - Rough effort: 3 dev days.
   - Owner suggestion: customer-success + observability.

Risk and open questions:
- Privacy / PII: need clear sanitize rules for exported sessions (PII removal, hashed ids). Consult security/compliance before shipping diagnostic export.
- UX expectations: customers may expect cache indicators to be exact; we must label them probabilistic where appropriate.
- Rollout complexity: soft-degrade policy interacts with existing routing and quota systems; require a compatibility matrix.

Quick experiments to validate signal before feature work:
- Add cache_hit tag to a small % of responses for selected customers and instrument it in CS dashboards for 2 weeks. Measure correlation with observed cost drops and customer satisfaction.
- Canary soft-degrade policy for one internal customer to observe quality delta vs. full fallback.

Handoff summary:
- Immediate quick wins: request-level cache signal + one-click diagnostic export + Console streaming toggle. These have low effort and unblock CS.
- Medium-term: soft-degrade fallback policy + tail-latency fast-shed runbook.
- Dependencies: privacy review, small Console UI changes, runtime flags.

Appendix: useful references and artifacts
- Link to recent incident timeline: slack://channel/C02ABCD9/thread-7f2
- Jira stub for cache signal experiment: JIRA-3912
- Confluence: field-voices-compact-sprint-briefing

Notes to PMs/Eng: prioritization guideline: baseline = (customer revenue sensitivity * incidence freq) + operational time saved. Use the quick experiments to gather signal before allocating larger sprints.

Last updated by: Ava Martinez (CS) — 2026-08-05.
